title: Apply for a provisional rider licence (unserviced area)
summary: Learn how to apply for a provisional (P1) rider licence in an unserviced area after passing a kerbside skills test.
intro:
To upgrade to a provisional (P1) rider licence in an unserviced area you must first pass a kerbside rider skills test.

You can book a kerbside rider skills test by visiting a Service NSW Centre or calling 13 22 13.

After passing the test, apply in person at a service centre for your provisional rider licence.

When you visit the service centre, you can apply for a NSW Photo Card at the same time, and pay a reduced application fee for it.
who_can_apply: Have held a learner rider licence for at least 3 months
Pass the kerbside rider skills test
what_you_need: Your contact lenses or glasses (if you wear them)

how_to_steps.text: Complete the form and check the tick box to apply for a Photo Card (if applicable).
Visit a service centre and lodge your application with your payment.

more_info.text: For rider licence applications, a receipt is provided which allows you to ride until the card arrives in the mail. The receipt is valid for 2 months.
The NSW Photo Card is voluntary – you don't have to have one, but you may find it useful to prove your identity in situations not related to riding/driving.

faqs.q: How do I start the process for a provisional rider licence in an unserviced area?
faqs.a: You must first pass a kerbside rider skills test. You can book this test by visiting a Service NSW Centre or calling 13 22 13.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a serviced and an unserviced area?
faqs.a: A serviced area is where motorcycle rider training is available, while an unserviced area is where there are no training providers within a reasonable distance.

faqs.q: What documents do I need to apply for the licence?
faqs.a: You need the 'Licence Application' PDF form, your learner rider licence, your contact lenses or glasses (if applicable), a current concession card (if applicable), and payment.
